thread.title: FCI Schuylkill inmate indicted for possession of a weapon
thread.title_full: FCI Schuylkill inmate indicted for possession of a weapon

author: Keystone Today
title: FCI Schuylkill inmate indicted for possession of a weapon
text:
Brayan Giron-Ferman, a 22-year-old federal inmate at FCI Schuylkill, was indicted by a federal grand jury on May 13 for possession of a weapon, according to the United States Attorney’s Office for the Middle District of Pennsylvania.
The case highlights ongoing concerns about safety and contraband within federal correctional facilities. Prosecutors allege that on February 27, Giron-Ferman possessed a prison-made weapon described as a seven-and-a-half-inch sharpened piece of metal with a cloth handle, commonly referred to as a “shank.”
United States Attorney Brian D. Miller said the Federal Bureau of Investigations and Special Investigative Services of the Federal Bureau of Prisons are investigating the matter. Assistant U.S. Attorney Luisa Honora Berti is prosecuting the case.
If convicted, Giron-Ferman faces up to five years in prison, supervised release after imprisonment, and a fine. Sentencing will be determined by the judge following consideration of federal sentencing statutes and guidelines.
The U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Middle District of Pennsylvania prosecutes federal crimes and manages civil cases in its jurisdiction covering 33 counties and serving about 3.2 million residents; it also offers victim support services and reentry programs that promote community safety through initiatives like Project Safe Neighborhoods according to the official website .
Officials emphasize that indictments are only allegations and all persons charged are presumed innocent unless found guilty in court.
